root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Declined: Langeheinicke Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 e3

overview: Black answers 4.f3 with the counter-thrust 4...e3, attacking the bishop on c1 and offering to give the pawn back. After 5.Bxe3 White has a free development and a big centre, and Black has kept ...Nf6 and a sound but passive game. It is a rare Blackmar-Diemer reply, so the details are unsure.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture with Bxe3 and develop quickly with Qd2, O-O-O or Bd3
Use the central pawns d4 and f3 to attack

black_ideas.idea: Use the d5 knight outpost and trade pieces

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4 against Black ...c5
White pawns on d4 and f3 against a Black d-file

character.notes: Black returns the pawn, but the game stays tactical with open lines and mutual piece play.

gambit.notes: Black takes e4 and returns the pawn on e3 with 5.Bxe3, so material is level and White is not a pawn down.

soundness.notes: Black is fine and White is not worse, so both sides play a sound game.

structure.notes: White d4 and f3 against open files, so mostly open.

approach.notes: The Blackmar-Diemer is seldom played by strong players, and this reply is rare too.

level.notes: Rare lines that need to be known.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main Blackmar-Diemer
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes on f3 instead and keeps the pawn, the real gambit.

character.reason: Open lines and a quick White development lead to tactical play for both sides.

gambit.reason: The pawn comes back with 5.Bxe3, so no material has been given up.

soundness.reason: Black returns the pawn and White gets an ordinary game.

structure.reason: The e-pawn trades open the centre.

approach.reason: The Blackmar-Diemer is rare among strong players.

level.reason: Narrow theory with tactics to know.

plans.reason: White gains time through the recapture and develops freely.
